reconcile.connective: Gill reconciles the reports two ways: Matthew's phrase can mean 'near' dead, and by the time Jairus reached Jesus he had rightly concluded she had died.

discrepancy.connective: Ehrman presses the objection directly: Matthew's aorist 'she has now died' cannot be softened to match Mark's still-living 'at the point of death.'

skeptic.name: Bart D. Ehrman
skeptic.work: "Are These Really Contradictions? My Response to Matt Firth," The Bart Ehrman Blog
skeptic.attribution: Bart D. Ehrman, "Are These Really Contradictions? My Response to Matt Firth," The Bart Ehrman Blog (April 22, 2019)

excerpts.excerpt_text: Her case seems to be differently represented; Mark says, she was "at the point of death", or "in the last extremity"; and Luke, that she "lay dying": but Matthew here says, that she was "even now dead", which may be easily reconciled: for not to observe, that signifies "near", and the phrase may be rendered, "she is near dead", or just expiring, the case was this; when Jairus left his house, his daughter was in the agony of death, just ready to give up the ghost; so, that he concluded, by the time he was with Jesus, she had made her exit; as it appears she had, by a messenger, who brought the account of her death, before they could get to the house.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Gill explicitly names all three synoptic phrasings ('at the point of death', 'lay dying', 'even now dead') and offers the standard two-part harmonization: a linguistic reading of Matthew's Greek as 'near' dead, plus a narrative-timing account in which Jairus's own belief that she had died (later confirmed by a messenger) updates between his departure and his address to Jesus.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible, note on Matthew 9:17 (1746-63)
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill treats this exact three-way tension directly under Matthew 9:17, harmonizing 'even now dead' with Mark's 'at the point of death' and Luke's 'lay dying' -- the same passage anchoring this row's reconcile pole; Haley's Alleged Discrepancies could not be confirmed to treat this specific passage.
